x: McMullen were some distance behind, walking together with Holland, Batson and Sandy. Derby and Birmingham were still scoring much better than either Belgrave or Surrey A.C, who made up the third and fourth placings.
They were then lost to sight whilst a lap of some 6 miles was traversed, and when again seen, the field was headed by Sandy, Surrey A.C., with Vickers, Sheffield, in close attendance.

Sandy (Surrey A.C.) and Vickers (Sheffield) dashed away at the start and at the five miles mark, at the top of a sharp hill, Sandy had a 200 yds. lead from the bunch who were to be concerned in the finish, consisting of Tommy Green, Plumb, Lloyd Johnson, Edge and Pretti, one of the Italian competitors.
